label: rem:hyperbolic-overlap-saturation
title: Hyperbolic-overlap strain saturation: the core aspect ratio locks at $\kappa^2 = \pi\nu/(2\Gamma+\pi\nu)$
html:
Once the stretching coordinate V_1 reaches the squared separation d^2, the point-vortex kernel breaks down. The local stream function shifts to a hyperbolic stagnation-point flow. The apparent flattening \kappa \to 0 reverses. The squared core aspect ratio locks to a strictly positive constant, \kappa^2 = \pi\nu/(2\Gamma + \pi\nu), rather than the naive quasi-steady Burgers ratio \pi\nu/\Gamma.

Mechanism of the kernel change. The singular Biot–Savart strain diverges because d \to 0. Once V_1 \gtrsim d^2, the filaments are no longer distinct. Their merged interaction is an elliptic-section vortex sitting at a hyperbolic stagnation point. The strain rate is bounded by the overlapping cores themselves. The length scale is \sqrt{V_1}. The kernel rotates to a Burgers-like strain \alpha_{\mathrm{hyp}}(t) = \Gamma/(\pi V_1(t)).

Saturated Townsend system. Substituting \alpha_{\mathrm{hyp}} into the stretching equation gives a constant right-hand side. V_1 grows linearly with time and remains finite through to the formal collision time T^\ast. The exponential runaway is replaced by controlled linear growth. The strain saturates because the same coordinate driving the stretching also sets the length scale.

Compression — proportionality ansatz. Substituting the saturated strain into the compression equation bounds the compressive sink. The V_2 relaxation rate is comparable to the V_1 growth rate, preventing quasi-steady equilibrium. Take the proportionality ansatz V_2(t) = \lambda V_1(t). The ODE forces

  \boxed{\;\;
  \kappa^2
  \;=\;
  \frac{V_2}{V_1}
  \;=\;
  \frac{\pi\nu}{2\Gamma + \pi\nu}.
  \;\;}

In the high-Reynolds limit, \kappa^2 \simeq \pi\nu/(2\Gamma).

Because \kappa^2 > 0, the cores do not flatten into sheets in this model: their cross-section locks into a finite ellipse.

Reading. The Biot–Savart prediction \kappa \to 0 is an artefact of the point-vortex approximation. The hyperbolic-overlap calculation predicts the asymptotic core ratio is strictly positive. The cores lock into a finite elliptical profile supported by the hyperbolic strain.

What the lock does not decide. The core aspect ratio carries no Levi information. With the plane field \ker\varTheta = \xi^\perp of The Levi datum of the vorticity plane field is the single scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi, the Levi datum is the single scalar \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi, and a straight anti-parallel pair has \xi\cdot\mathrm{curl}\,\xi = 0 whatever its core shape. So \kappa^2 > 0 does not establish Levi non-degeneracy, and by itself it carries no blow-up verdict; inferring finite-time blow-up of classical 3D Navier–Stokes from non-degenerate Levi data alone is refuted by steady Beltrami counterexamples (Levi degeneracy conjecture).

Caveats.

  1. The kernel switch at the overlap time is a phenomenological dimensional ansatz, not a derivation from Euler/NS.
  2. The asymptotic value is the attracting proportionality ratio, not the naive Burgers equilibrium.
  3. The Townsend equations assume axisymmetric straining. Three-dimensional instabilities may modify the picture.
  4. The explicit ODE establishes the asymptotic core-shape constant and nothing more. No route from this constant to blow-up remains in the chapter.
